slides.headline: Your first order is closer than you think
Start with people who know you
slides.text: Friends, family, church, old classmates. Send each one a personal message about one product, not a long list.

slides.headline: Have these ready before you post
Myth: you need many followers first
slides.text: Truth: one person who trusts you can be your first order. Start with your contacts, then grow.
About how long Rex takes to build your store from a chat. Then you have a link to share.

slides.do: Reply fast and say the price clearly
slides.dont: Reply “DM for price” and leave buyers guessing

slides.headline: Open your shop today
slides.text: Take the Academy track Start your shop: short lessons from your first product to a store link you can share.

slides.headline: Your Status is your shop window
Post a little, every day
slides.text: A few clear updates spread through the day keep you in view without flooding your contacts.

slides.headline: Myth: more posts always mean more sales
slides.text: Truth: twenty posts in a row get skipped. A few clear posts with prices get read.

slides.headline: Always show the price
slides.text: “DM for price” makes people scroll past. Put the price, sizes and how to order on the picture.

slides.do: Add your store link so people can order at night
slides.dont: Repost blurry screenshots from your supplier’s Status

slides.headline: Turn views into orders
slides.text: The Academy track Sell on WhatsApp covers Status, broadcasts, quick replies and follow-ups.

slides.headline: Price for profit, not just for sales
Count every cost
slides.text: Product, packaging, delivery you cover, payment fees and your time. Skip one and your profit quietly disappears.
Buy at ₦8,000, sell at ₦12,000. That leaves ₦4,000 before delivery and fees. Know this number.
Payment fee on a ₦10,000 order: 1.5% is ₦150, plus ₦100. Fees are capped at ₦2,000.
Payment fee on a ₦2,000 order: 1.5% is ₦30. The ₦100 is waived on orders under ₦2,500.

slides.headline: Myth: the cheapest seller always wins
slides.text: Truth: buyers also pay for trust, fast replies and safe delivery. Compete on service, not only price.

slides.headline: Work out your price
slides.text: Use the free selling price calculator on shopinbos.com to set prices that leave real profit.

slides.headline: Good photos sell before you type
Use daylight, not flash
slides.text: Stand near a window in the morning or late afternoon. Soft light shows the real colour.

slides.do: Use a plain background, like a white wall
slides.dont: Shoot on a busy bed with clothes everywhere

slides.headline: Myth: you need an expensive camera
slides.text: Truth: a clean phone lens, good light and a steady hand are enough for most products.

slides.headline: Show the size
slides.text: Hold the bag, wear the shoe, put the jar beside a phone. Buyers want to picture it in real life.

slides.headline: Make listings that sell
slides.text: The Academy track Instagram, TikTok and ads has lessons on photos and short videos that bring buyers.

slides.headline: Pay on delivery, without the wahala
Why buyers ask for it
slides.text: Many buyers have been burnt by online shops before. Paying when the item arrives makes a new shop feel safe.
Shopinbos pay on delivery covers orders up to ₦50,000 in Lagos, Abuja, Ibadan and Port Harcourt.
Every pay on delivery order has a 4-digit code. The customer gives it to the rider when they pay.
Riders pay the cash in by 6pm the same day. Your balance goes to your bank every Friday.

slides.do: Message to confirm the order before dispatch
slides.dont: Send big orders to numbers that never pick up

slides.headline: Get paid, every time
slides.text: Take Get paid and deliver in the Academy: pay on delivery, transfers, riders and refunds, without wahala.

slides.headline: Clear, careful delivery brings buyers back
Say the delivery time upfront
slides.text: Put your real delivery time on every product. Clear promises stop endless “where is my order?” messages.

slides.headline: No surprise costs
slides.text: Shopinbos shows the delivery price at checkout, so buyers see the full cost before they pay.
Item ₦12,000 plus delivery ₦1,500. The buyer sees ₦13,500 at checkout, so nobody argues at the gate.

slides.do: Send the rider’s details to your customer
slides.dont: Go quiet once the parcel leaves

slides.headline: Plan your deliveries
slides.text: Book riders straight from the order in Shopinbos, and learn more in the Academy track Get paid and deliver.

slides.headline: Sell products without buying stock first
How it works
slides.text: You list a supplier’s product in your store. A buyer orders, and the supplier ships with your shop’s label.

slides.headline: Myth: dropshipping is free money
slides.text: Truth: you still do the selling. Posts, replies and customer care are your job.
Supplier price ₦6,500, your price ₦10,000. ₦3,500 is yours before fees and marketing.

slides.do: Order a sample and check the quality yourself
slides.dont: List hundreds of products you have never seen

slides.headline: Find stock to sell
slides.text: Browse checked Nigerian suppliers in Shopinbos, then take the Academy track Find stock and dropship.

slides.headline: Short videos show what photos can’t
Hook them in the first seconds
slides.text: Open with the product in action or the problem it solves. Keep the long intro for later, or skip it.

slides.headline: Myth: you must dance to sell
slides.text: Truth: simple, clear videos of the product, with the price on screen, can sell well.

slides.headline: Make it easy to buy
slides.text: Put your store link in your bio and say “link in bio”. Don’t make buyers hunt for how to order.

slides.do: Reply quickly to comments asking “how much?”
slides.dont: Hide the price and wait for DMs

slides.headline: Grow on social
slides.text: The Academy track Instagram, TikTok and ads covers photos, short videos and small ads that bring the right people.

slides.headline: Your next order can come from old buyers
Follow up after delivery
slides.text: Two or three days later, send a short message: “Did it arrive well? How are you finding it?”
One customer who spends ₦10,000 every month is worth ₦120,000 a year. Look after them.

slides.headline: Simple ways to bring them back
Myth: happy buyers come back on their own
slides.text: Truth: people forget. A friendly WhatsApp message when new stock lands often brings them back.

slides.do: Save every buyer’s name and what they bought
slides.dont: Add customers to broadcasts without asking first

slides.headline: Keep customers coming back
slides.text: Take Grow and keep customers in the Academy: discounts, loyalty and the simple numbers that show what’s working.

slides.headline: Get ready before the rush, not during
Stock up early
slides.text: Suppliers and markets get busy before Christmas and Sallah. Order your best sellers weeks ahead, not days.
Sell a ₦9,000 perfume and a ₦6,000 body lotion as a ₦13,500 gift set. The buyer saves ₦1,500.

slides.headline: Myth: December sells itself
slides.text: Truth: everybody else is selling too. Plan your posts, offers and delivery dates early to stand out.

slides.do: Post your last order date for delivery before the holiday
slides.dont: Promise Christmas Eve delivery you can’t keep

slides.headline: Plan your season
slides.text: The Academy track Grow and keep customers shows how to plan offers, discounts and follow-ups.
